title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Playbook for Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Sofia Martinez
summary: This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation processes: how to configure and run the eval harness, construct and maintain prompt sets and benchmarks, onboard new models for serving, enforce quality guardrails, apply quantization profiles safely, and run a structured regression triage process.
body:
Overview:
This document is the canonical reference for applied-ML engineers and product partners running model evaluations and quality guardrails for Redwood Inference. It combines guidance, concrete CLI examples, acceptance thresholds, ownership, and actionable runbooks for investigating regressions. The goal is a reproducible, auditable path from model candidate -> eval -> gating -> production rollout with quantization and regression safeguards.

Scope:
- Eval harness (integration and CI usage)
- Prompt sets and benchmark design, versioning, and bias/safety checks
- Model onboarding checklist from candidate submission through canary rollout
- Quality guardrails: automated checks and manual review triggers
- Quantization profile catalog and safe rollout parameters
- Regression triage playbook and escalation matrix

Goals and high-level SLOs:
1) Prevent detectable quality regressions: automated eval suite must pass a per-prompt-set delta threshold (see Acceptance Criteria).
2) Keep 95th-percentile inference latency within target for each class of instance and quantization profile.
3) Make model onboarding reproducible and auditable with clear ownership and rollback criteria.

Ownership and roles:
- Applied ML (owner): maintains eval harness, prompt-set repo, scoring scripts, and quantization profiles.
- Serving Runtime (owner): implements kernel/quantization runtime changes and provides perf telemetry.
- Product/Feature Owner: supplies canonical prompt sets, business criteria, and correctness priorities.
- Release Manager: approves production rollouts and controls canary windows.

Eval Harness: setup and CI integration
- Repository: infra lives in git: git@repo:redwood/applied-ml/eval-harness.git
- CLI (example):
  - Install (recommended in CI): pip install -r requirements.txt && python -m pip install .
  - Run evaluations locally: rwi-eval run --config configs/benchmark-suite.yaml --model candidate-v2 --output results/candidate-v2.json
  - Run deterministic replay for a failing test: rwi-eval replay --input results/candidate-v2.json --seed 12345
- CI integration: include rwi-eval run in PR checks for model-onboarding branch. A green CI is required for staged rollout.
- Artifacting: evaluation artifacts (raw outputs, token-level logs, and scorecards) must be uploaded to S3 at s3://redwood-evals/<model>/<run-id>/ with lifecycle tagging (retain 90 days by default).

Prompt Sets and Benchmarks: guidelines and structure
- Organization: Prompt sets are stored in prompt-sets/ with a manifest (YAML) that lists intent, difficulty, expected outputs, and canonical labels. Each prompt set must include metadata: owner, business_priority (P0/P1/P2), creation_date, and related_feature_id.
- Diversity and size guidance: production intent sets >= 500 prompts; unit-level microbenchmarks (ads, code, summarization) >= 100 prompts.
- Labeling: ground-truth labels are necessary where applicable (classification, QA). For open-ended generation, provide 3 human references and an evaluation rubric.
- Versioning: Use semantic version tags on the manifest (e.g., v1.2.0). Back-compatibility: changes that add prompts are patch-level; changes to rubrics or scoring are minor/major and require re-evaluation of previously approved models.
- Safety / bias checks: include a toxicity and PII detection pass using the safety pipeline. Any prompt set with >2% toxicity triggers a manual review.

Model Onboarding Checklist (from candidate to canary)
1) Candidate submission: PR with model binary location, config, quantization compatibility notes, and benchmark results.
2) Automated checks: eval harness run against canonical prompt sets, perf sweep (latency/throughput/kv-cache tests), and smoke safety checks.
3) Human review: applied-ml reviewer verifies failure modes, sampling of outputs, and rubric scores.
4) Staging deploy (canary): 5-10% traffic for 24-72 hours with monitoring on key metrics.
5) Production rollout: progressive rollout guided by automated rollback policies.
6) Post-rollout evaluation: re-run evaluation harness against live traffic traces and prompt sets.

Acceptance Criteria and Quality Guardrails
- Pass / fail thresholds are defined per prompt set in the manifest. Standard thresholds:
  - Mean rubric score delta <= -0.05 (candidate vs baseline) for pass.
  - Safety: false positive rate for safety filters <= baseline + 1.5% absolute.
  - Regression budget: no more than 1% of critical prompts may drop below critical-score threshold.
- Performance budgets (example):
  - Baseline model (non-quantized): p50 latency <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms (for 8k context workloads on 80GB GPU).
  - Quantized int8 profile target: p50 <= 100ms, p95 <= 300ms, with quality delta constraint described above.
- Manual gating: any single critical prompt failure that causes wrong legal/safety advice or data leakage triggers an immediate rollback.

Quantization Profiles: catalog and safe rollout
- Profiles are named and versioned. Minimal catalog example:
  - qfp-int8-v1: symmetric per-tensor int8, recommended for encoder-decoder and decoder-only models where QA acceptability delta <= 0.03.
  - qfp-ptq-8g-v1: post-training quantization with group size 128, fallback to float16 for attention kernels when divergence detected.
  - qfp-fast-fp16-v1: optimized fp16 kernel packing for low-latency workloads.
- Profile metadata fields (manifest): profile_name, quant_bits, group_size, applicable_architectures, expected_quality_delta, monitored_metrics, owner.
- Safe rollout pattern:
  1) Local evals with selected prompt sets (smoke + domain-specific).
  2) Perf sweep: batch sizes and latency measured on dedicated infra (gpu-fleet/perf-sweeps job).
  3) Staging canary: 1% traffic with A/B vs baseline for 48h.
  4) Automated gating: must meet acceptance criteria (quality + perf). If quality delta above limit or safety filters increase, immediately block.
- Telemetry to monitor: token-level mismatch rate, generation entropy shift, perplexity delta, toxicity flag rate, latency p50/p95.

Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)
- Trigger sources: automated CI failures, monitoring alert, customer report, or internal audit.
- Initial triage (15-30 minutes):
  1) Owner/first-responder acknowledges and creates incident in Ops (link to runbook).
  2) Gather artifacts: model version, eval-harness results, prompt-set identifiers, recent config changes, rollout window, and SLO deltas.
  3) Run deterministic replay: rwi-eval replay --input <artifact> --seed <seed> to confirm reproducibility.
- Classification matrix:
  - Type A (Quality regression): automatic evaluation shows delta > threshold and reproduced locally.
  - Type B (Perf regression): latency or error-rate increase without quality delta.
  - Type C (Safety regression): safety filter escalation or new PII leakage pattern.
- Remediation patterns:
  - For Type A: rollback to previous model, open regression bug with model and eval teams, create new prompt tests covering failure modes.
  - For Type B: investigate infra/kernel/quantization changes; if correlated with deploy, revert runtime change.
  - For Type C: immediate rollback + incident response with security and compliance.
- Escalation matrix:
  - If more than 5% of critical prompts fail -> Escalate to Eng-SRE + Product director within 1 hour.
  - If customer-impacting or SLA breach -> engage customer success and legal within 2 hours.

Operational Playbook: quick commands and dashboards
- Fast checks:
  - Check latest artifacts: aws s3 ls s3://redwood-evals/<model>/ --profile evals
  - Run regen slice locally: rwi-eval run --manifest prompt-sets/critical.yaml --model candidate --limit 100
  - Perf probe: perf-sweep run --model candidate --profile qfp-int8-v1 --batch 8 --duration 300s
- Dashboards (owners):
  - Eval Scorecard (per-model): rubric means, delta to baseline, token-mismatch heatmap.
  - Safety Dashboard: toxicity rate, PII detections, policy-violations grouped by prompt set.
  - Quantization Perf: p50/p95 by profile, kernel fallback counts, memory usage.

Auditing and Compliance
- All onboarding runs must attach an audit record containing: model binary hash, eval artifact S3 path, prompt-set manifest version, reviewers, and approval timestamp.
- Retention: artifacts retained for 90 days by default; critical customer-related artifacts retained for 3 years (handled by Compliance team).

Appendix: Example prompt-set manifest snippet (YAML, shown as literal)
- name: critical-invoice-parsing
  version: v1.0.0
  owner: product-invoice
  business_priority: P0
  size: 750
  rubric: |
    - correctness: binary match on invoice fields (0/1)
    - tolerance: date formats normalized
  safety_checks: [toxicity, pii_detection]

notes: This playbook is intentionally prescriptive: automated checks are first-class gates and manual review is reserved for exceptional cases. Keep prompt sets and quantization manifests under source control and require PR reviews for all changes.
